subject: science
skillName: Habitats and Which Organisms Can Survive

items.prompt:
A habitat is
A) the place where an organism lives
B) a kind of food
C) a type of weather only
D) a fossil
items.answer: A) the place where an organism lives

steps: A habitat is where an organism lives, with its conditions.

items.prompt:
In a dry desert, a cactus would
A) survive well
B) not survive at all
C) need lots of water
D) drown

steps: A cactus is suited to dry conditions.

items.prompt:
In a dry desert, a water lily would
A) survive well
B) not survive, because it needs lots of water
C) grow faster
D) make its own water
items.answer: B) not survive, because it needs lots of water

steps: The desert lacks the water the lily needs.

items.prompt:
Why can some organisms survive in a habitat and others cannot?
A) Their needs match the conditions or do not
B) All organisms survive everywhere
C) No organism can survive anywhere
D) It is random
items.answer: A) Their needs match the conditions or do not

items.prompt:
In a cold snowy habitat, which survives better?
A) A polar bear
B) A warmth-needing lizard
C) A water lily
D) A cactus

steps: The polar bear is suited to the cold.

items.prompt:
On a shady forest floor, which plant survives well?
A) A sun-needing plant
B) A shade-loving plant
C) A cactus
D) A water lily

steps: The shade-loving plant matches the shady conditions.

items.prompt:
In one habitat, it is true that
A) all organisms survive equally
B) some thrive, some do poorly, and some cannot survive
C) no organism survives
D) only plants survive
items.answer: B) some thrive, some do poorly, and some cannot survive

steps: Survival varies with how well organisms match the habitat.

items.prompt:
The BEST argument that a fish cannot survive in a desert is that
A) deserts are hot
B) a fish needs water to breathe and the desert has none
C) fish are small
D) deserts have sand
items.answer: B) a fish needs water to breathe and the desert has none

steps: No water means the fish cannot survive, matching needs to the habitat.
